subject: Mediva RFP: cross-border evidence & DPA annex coordination
messages:
From: Suzanne Park <suzanne.park@medivahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: RFP follow-up: technical evidence for cross-border transfers and DPA annex

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call last week. As part of our vendor diligence for the Mediva inference procurement (RFP #MED-2026-088), Legal and Procurement need a concise evidence pack focused on cross-border transfers and the DPA annex. We want to close the compliance review by Jan 22.

Can you provide a single package that covers:
- The legal mechanism you rely on for EU->US transfers (are you using SCCs, transfers based on adequacy, or a DPF approach?)
- The DPA annex you propose for Mediva (we need to review annex clauses mapping to subprocessors, retention, audit rights)
- Operational controls: KMS usage, key residency options, replay/log access (audit logs), and retention/erasure flows for inference KV cache and telemetry
- Evidence of subprocessor limits / how you notify customers of changes
- A point of contact for SOC2 or audit evidence requests (if we need attestation or evidence)

If possible please include an attachment stub and a brief narrative (1 page) we can share with our data protection team. Also flag any constraints for highly regulated PHI workloads.

Best,
Suzanne
Suzanne Park
Head of Legal Operations, Mediva Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Suzanne Park <suzanne.park@medivahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: technical evidence for cross-border transfers and DPA annex

Hi Suzanne — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a first-pass evidence pack and a proposed DPA annex for Mediva. High-level summary below; the attachments contain clause-level mapping and operational screenshots where relevant.

Summary (top-line):
- Transfer mechanism: Redwood supports European controller/customer deployments with three options: (1) EU-hosted region (data residency) for private deployments; (2) Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for hosted API traffic with EU origin -> US processing; (3) Data Processing Framework (DPF) supplement for enterprise customers who require demonstrable contractual and technical controls consistent with DPF principles. The attached SCCs+DPF matrix shows how we map controls to Mediva's questions.
- DPA Annex: Draft included (Redwood_DPA_Annex_Mediva_v1.1.docx). It includes subprocessor list, processing location clauses, audit and notice timelines, key management options, and retention scoping. We left flaggable placeholders where Mediva may want narrower residency/retention terms.
- KMS/key residency: Customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK) on Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed KMS but with customer-specific key-splitting/rotations on request under enterprise contracts. Annex has KMS integration appendix.
- KV cache & telemetry: By default caching metadata (prefix/KV) resides in the same region as the compute; for hosted where origin is EU and processing happens in US we offer cache residency controls via token-routing policies and can configure cache flush/ttl settings. We documented default retention windows and the erasure flow (delete jobs + audit log entry).
- Subprocessors: Full list included; we commit 30 days' advance notice for new subprocessors and a dedicated notifications feed (link in attachments).
- Audit & SOC2: Point of contact for audit evidence: Monica Patel, Security & Compliance. We can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA and coordinate a targeted controls walk-through.

Attachments included (stubs):
- CrossBorder_Evidence_Pack_Mediva.pdf (control maps, KMS screenshots, cache flow diagrams)
- Redwood_DPA_Annex_Mediva_v1.1.docx (annotated annex draft)
- SCCs_and_DPF_Matrix.xlsx (mapping of SCC/DPA/DPF controls to questions)

Next steps: If you can flag any items you want tightened (e.g., mandatory EU-only processing, additional deletion SLAs), we’ll mark them in the annex and return a redline. We’re available for a 30–45m call with engineering and compliance the week of Jan 19.

Regards,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Compliance (Sales)
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: CrossBorder_Evidence_Pack_Mediva.pdf; Redwood_DPA_Annex_Mediva_v1.1.docx; SCCs_and_DPF_Matrix.xlsx
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivahealth.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:47:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: technical evidence for cross-border transfers and DPA annex

Thanks Stephanie — the pack looks useful. A couple quick clarifications before we circulate to our DPO:

1) KV cache residency: You mention cache can be co-located with compute or routed by policy. For EU-origin requests routed to Redwood hosted endpoints in the US, can you confirm whether any customer prompt context or partial KV is persisted in US-only storage by default? We need a short statement of default behavior and whether we can enforce EU-only KV retention for our account.

2) Audit artifacts: For erasure jobs and key rotations we need the log artifact format. Do you provide a tamper-evident log or signed attestations? Alternatively, are you able to provide an exportable audit package for a particular date range?

If you could reply with short, two-line answers we can decide whether to run this through Legal or escalate to our Security team.

Thanks,
Tom
Procurement Lead, Mediva Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@medivahealth.com>, Suzanne Park <suzanne.park@medivahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 15:48:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: technical evidence for cross-border transfers and DPA annex (answers)

Tom / Suzanne — quick answers below; see attached PDF for screenshots and export sample. If you want an on-record attestation we can schedule a short SOC2 supplement call (Monica).

- KV cache residency (two lines): Default hosted behavior: transient KV/prefix cache is stored in the same region as the inference compute. For EU-origin traffic routed to US-hosted compute, minimal cache artifacts (tokenized prefixes + routing metadata) are persisted in the US by default. For Mediva, we can enforce EU-only KV residency via routing policy + tenancy pin (will require dedicated routing rule; documented as an optional configuration in the annex).

- Audit artifacts (two lines): We publish exportable audit bundles (JSON + CSV) for erasure jobs, key-rotation events, and deletion confirmations. Audit bundles are signed with a rotating HMAC and include per-event sequence numbers; for higher assurance we offer time-stamped attestations (signed by our KMS) under an enterprise addendum.

Action items I’ll own:
- Karthik: add a short appendix to the annex that enumerates the exact config steps to pin cache residency and associated billing/latency tradeoffs.
- Monica: attach SOC2 request flow and the NDA template for sharing the Type II report.

We’ve attached: CrossBorder_Evidence_Pack_Mediva.pdf (updated), Redwood_DPA_Annex_Mediva_v1.1.docx (annotated v1.1), SCCs_and_DPF_Matrix.xlsx.

Let us know availability for a technical+compliance call Jan 20–22; we can push earlier if helpful.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Director, Customer Compliance (Sales)
Redwood Inference
